thread:
Priya: ok team, quick brain dump — I want to prototype a small "postmortem triage" bot. Trigger when PD marks RESOLVED, produce a draft PM, prefill impact/estimated customers using metrics, and push action items to our action-dashboard. Keep it editable, not auto-publish. Thoughts?
Diego: sounds useful. main risk: false positives on customer-impact. how do we avoid garbage data getting locked into the draft?
Priya: plan is heuristics + confidence score. pull PD timeline + Redwood metrics (5xx rate, p50/p95 lat, error budget burn). Prefill with numbers and confidence, owner can edit inline before publish.
Rory: make sure template varies by severity. map severity -> template. also include a quick meeting scheduler button (15/30/60) in the draft message.
Ava: UX: DM the on-call with a summary + suggested owner, but require explicit confirm (buttons: Confirm owner, Change owner). no auto-assign.
Sam: implementation idea: a slash command `/pm-triage <incident-id>` plus an autotrigger on PD resolve. autotrigger should create a draft in #pm-drafts and DM oncall rather than publish. have action buttons in the draft: [Review & Publish] [Edit Draft].
Priya: yes. add TTL: if no action in 48h escalate to SRE lead. the escalation should also surface in the action-dashboard as a high-priority card.
oncall-bot: Incident 1799998888 was RESOLVED by @Ava at 2026-03-14T18:25Z — create draft postmortem? [Yes] [No]
Ava: clicked Yes, show me the draft please.
pm-bot: Draft created: https://redwood.internal/pm-drafts/1799998888 — template: sev-2-runtime-deg — prefilled customer_impact: "~420 customers saw >40% latency increase for ~11m" (conf: 0.69). suggested owner: @Diego. suggested meeting: tomorrow 09:30 PT.
Diego: decent. i'll review and pull product + cs. confidence metric is useful. we should allow a tiny inline modal to tweak numbers so owners don't need to jump to the doc.
Priya: agreed. modal fields: affected_customers_est, duration_minutes, root_error_class. also record an audit entry of edits (who/ts).
Rory: for action items, create an action-dashboard card per task with metadata: incident_id, owner, due_date, severity-derived-priority. that lets us query regressions later.
Sam: i can own the Slack flow + modal. Diego, you take PD + metrics ingestion and severity heuristics. i'll add a feature-flag to gate autotrigger.
Diego: tighten RBAC: bot needs read PD + metrics, write to action-dashboard and PM drafts. use a service account with minimal scopes. we'll add an infra checklist.
Priya: good. config: an opt-out list for noisy monitors (synth checks) in /infra/pm-triage/config.yaml. also retention: drafts older than 90 days archive automatically. published PMs get copied into our docs repo with PII/customer list obfuscated.
Ava: CSMs: if an incident has user-visible impact, notify #customer-success with a short summary and link to the PM. include a checkbox in the draft "notify CSMs".
Diego: edge case: multi-region incidents where different teams own different impact slices. MVP: support single-owner; multi-owner -> v2.
Priya: MVP scope: slash command + draft generation + basic heuristics + action-card creation + modal edit + DM confirm + escalation TTL. target ~5w. v2 adds multi-region + auto-publish templates.
Sam: testing: add an e2e fixture that simulates PD resolve -> bot draft -> owner confirms -> card created. include deterministic metrics fixture.
Rory: rollout: internal alpha for eng-oncall + SRE for 2 weeks, measure: time to first edit, publish rate, percent actions created. collect qualitative feedback.
Diego: telemetry: track draft_confidence, edits_per_draft, publish_latency, escalation_rate. useful to tune heuristics.
Priya: follow-up infra tasks: create service principal, RBAC doc, config file, and QA plan. i'll open the main ticket and tag owners.
Ava: tiny UX ask: include a one-line incident summary in the DM (title + quick bullets) so oncall can triage faster.
Sam: i'll sketch the slash modal and a sample webhook payload by EOD. Diego, can you draft the severity heuristics doc for tomorrow's 11am review?
Diego: yep.
Priya: thanks team. i'll track the owners and timeline. excited to see if this cuts PM latency. :rocket:
